name: detail-solo-consistency
note: UAT batch 3 items 4+6. RED-FIRST vs main: (a) the song view's back wore .backArrowBtn (accent-filled) while the Studio's wore a bare .iconBtn (surface-2) - two looks for one meaning, so the computed-background equality below fails; (b) the Studio's fly-out trigger was a hamburger sitting exactly where the app Settings gear lives, on a screen that COVERS the appbar (the operator flagged that slot twice); (c) the large sheet chord chips were inert <span>s, so the tagName/data-c asserts fail. Geometry is measured with offsetWidth/offsetHeight, never getBoundingClientRect, because the rect is the TRANSFORMED box and a chip's own :active scale(.9) makes a compliant 44px control read 39.6px.

steps.label: song view back composes the shared primitive (.iconBtn.backArrowBtn), 44x44
record the song view's back look + its offset INSIDE its own header, so the Studio's is compared against a MEASURED value rather than a hardcoded colour that would rot with the accent theme
the overflow trigger is top-RIGHT on the song view - the slot the Studio must mirror
layout settle gate: await document.fonts.ready before any geometry assert
UAT item 6: every large sheet chord chip is a real, keyboard-focusable button (was an inert <span>)
each large chip carries the CANONICAL token to play plus an accessible name that states the chord it sounds
the button box inherits the sheet's type scale - a <button> inherits NO font, so a missing font:inherit would drop these ~27px chips to the ~13px UA default and nothing else would complain
visible large chips clear the 44px tap floor on BOTH axes (zero-box chips filtered FIRST so a hidden one cannot fake a pass)
turning the chips into buttons did not push the page into horizontal overflow

UAT item 4: the Studio's back is the SAME control - same classes, same computed fill/ink/radius, same 44x44 box, same glyph, and the same LEADING slot in its own header row. Position is compared header-relative, not viewport-relative: the song view's header sits inside a padded card and the Studio's is a full-bleed sheet, so an absolute-x gate would encode the card padding rather than the claim, and would fail on a design that is in fact consistent
